title: Declare named themes on every train; keep them out of the train id

facts.note: Planning task mentions trains or themes; the rule applies to every train regardless of edit type.
Plan artifacts and the theme taxonomy source. Not assumed exhaustive: a train defined anywhere is in scope, so path matching is a hint, not a gate.
Needs a diff/artifact-level observer that recognises train definitions wherever they live and flags any added or modified train.
A plan validator would check every train for themes and typed identity.

fires: Planner edits any part of an existing train (themes, id, wagons list, description or other metadata).
Planner reviews or validates the plan and its trains.
A train definition appears in any artifact, inside or outside the plan directory.
doesNotFire: Work that neither defines, edits nor reviews any train (e.g. code changes containing no train definition).

given: A train exists in, or is being added to, the plan.
when: The planner authors, edits or reviews that train.
then: Declare one or more named themes on the train, using the repository-defined theme taxonomy (source: plan/_themes.yaml).
prefer: Treat themes as named plan metadata that classifies the journey the train covers.
Keep the train identity in the typed form train:{subject}:{slug}.
Take theme values from the taxonomy as defined: it reserves zero as commons (reserved_zero = commons) and other values are repository-defined; do not infer further semantics for the reserved value.
avoid: Encoding a theme in the train identity (e.g. a theme number or theme prefix in the id); digits that do not encode a theme are not affected.
Reviving the retired numeric theme-range scheme to derive or reserve train ids.
Leaving a train with no declared theme.
why: Themes classify the journey, while identity is the typed train:{subject}:{slug}; keeping them separate means classification is metadata and is never encoded in identity.
evidence: Every train in the plan declares one or more named themes (in whatever representation the plan uses).
Declared themes are values of the repository-defined theme taxonomy whose source is plan/_themes.yaml.
Train ids match train:{subject}:{slug} and contain no theme encoding.
verifier_detail: Term theme_taxonomy (label 'Themes'): themes are repository-defined plan metadata; values.source = plan/_themes.yaml; values.reserved_zero = commons; values.other_values = repository-defined. The source states no further semantics for reserved_zero.
Theme is metadata, not identity: validate train id against train:{subject}:{slug} independently of themes; only theme-encoding in the id is a finding, not the mere presence of digits.

Graph edges (theme-alignment reads primary theme from first train-id digit; theme ranges span four categories) reflect the retired numeric scheme and may be stale relative to this convention.

splitSuggestion.then: Keep train identity as train:{subject}:{slug} with no theme encoded in it.

additions.text: The source carries two obligations: declare named themes (then) and keep themes out of train identity (avoid/prefer here). A separate convention planner.train.identity-excludes-theme could own the identity obligation.
Leaving a train with no declared theme.
additions.justification: Direct negation of the source's 'Each train declares one or more named themes'; stated as an anti-pattern for clarity.

additions.text: Clarification that digits not encoding a theme are not affected.
additions.justification: Prevents over-reading the identity anti-pattern as a ban on all digits; the source only forbids encoding themes in identity.

additions.text: Note that graph edges reflect the retired numeric scheme.
additions.justification: Helps auditors reconcile graph.json reasons with the source's divergence_note.
